title: The Original Hexagon: The First Cell

features.name: the counting begins
features.desc-on-touch: You place your hand on the first hexagon where counting was invented, where the singular cell learned it could divide. The mathematics is warm, patient, not yet infinite.

features.name: the bee-scribe's ledger
features.desc-on-touch: A standing directory listing carved into honeycomb paper shows the first numbers ever written. The handwriting is deliberate, pre-decimal, from a time when counting had weight.

features.name: pollen-drift archive
features.desc-on-touch: Dust suspended in light shows the memory of bees carrying the first enumeration back to their hexagons. This is where the archive learned it could be distributed.

features.name: the still-unbroken cell
features.desc-on-touch: One hexagon remains intact, untouched by division or replication. It is sealed. You can feel the pressure of everything it contains: the one before the many.

features.name: the original colony mark
features.desc-on-touch: A symbol pressed into wax by something that had never before thought to mark itself. The mark is so old it has become a hieroglyph.

inscription: before the cell divided, there was only one, and its counting was enough
